sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: *Hol*? asks where someone or something is. The location phrase normally comes before van in a simple location sentence.

items.english: The book is on the table.

sections.content: Think of van as the period at the end of a Hungarian sentence about where something is — the location comes first because that’s the actual news, and van just confirms it’s true. English does the opposite, front-loading ‘is’ before we even say where. Once this flips in your head, forming these sentences gets much faster.
